idiom_name: trait plus class composition; Scala 3 export clauses for generated forwarding
implementation_notes: In Scala the letter is a trait and the envelope a class that extends it, either with explicit overrides or, from Scala 3, with an `export` clause that creates final aliases for the delegate's members - the language documentation presents export clauses as making composition as concise as inheritance, replacing a sequence of hand-written forwarders, and members can be renamed or omitted while exporting. Because export aliases are final and cannot override concrete members, the delegate is fixed and cannot be intercepted; runtime swapping needs an ordinary field plus explicit overrides, and Scala 2 has no export at all, so the hand-written envelope is still the right form there or whenever individual calls must be adapted.
pitfalls: Export aliases are final and cannot override concrete members of base classes, so exporting and intercepting the same member is impossible - interception means an explicit override.
Export requires a stable path: a constructor parameter must be a val to be exportable, and exporting a var re-reads it per call while exporting a val freezes the delegate.
Scala 2 has no export clause, so the same design degenerates into a list of forwarders that drifts from the trait whenever it changes.
